open_items_before_freeze: owner re-decision with corrected numbers: (a) target grid configuration (tail replicates), informed by the v2 paired power simulation; (b) the review calendar tolerance D_max from which the ruling ceiling is mechanically derived
owner ratifications: the no-replacement rule for failed new judges; the preregistered tolerant anchor parse as a NEW phase-3 rule; the S1 downturn secondary contrast

source_bindings.hash_convention: canonical_sha256 (rejudge.phase2_execution.canonical_sha256) for JSON artifacts; raw-bytes sha256 for non-JSON files

unit_definitions.cell: one (question, judge, debater, condition) combination BEFORE transcript/side/replicate expansion; used only for grid bookkeeping in this document
unit_definitions.slot: one fully-expanded judgment unit (question, judge, debater, condition, transcript, side, replicate); the provider-billed unit
unit_definitions.completion_rule: every completion policy and completion gate in this protocol is defined at the SLOT level, using the slot totals for the selected configuration and final roster size (see debate_grid.slot_arithmetic_by_roster); never at the cell level

question_set.identical_to: phase2_protocol.json question_set (same three banks, same hashes, same 24 calibration exclusions, same 82 main questions)

transcript_reuse.policy: phase 3 makes ZERO debater calls. All judged debates are the phase-2 uncapped blind transcripts reused byte-identical: the budget affects only the judge, and the debater prompts never state a numeric budget, so transcripts are budget-agnostic by construction.

main_bundle.content: the 492 uncapped blind debate transcripts (82 questions x 2 self-play debaters x 3 transcripts) generated under phase-2 execution identity ba017fe3c6753a79236917b932b5434a8b99b9e2de37f0d32d4aca38f6613c1c
main_bundle.materialization: extract into a canonical transcript bundle with sha256; verify EVERY transcript (100% coverage, never sampled) against the phase-2 hash-chained result store before the bundle freezes; the manifest binds the bundle hash
main_bundle.verifier: internal QA by the orchestrating assistant (not an independent audit); the verification report (per-transcript hashes, source store event hashes) is a tracked artifact the owner can spot-check

canary_bundle.content: the phase-2 bridge-canary uncapped transcripts for the 24 held-out questions (one per question per debater)
canary_bundle.materialization: same 100% extraction-and-verification rule; if any held-out transcript cannot be verifiably extracted, generating a replacement canary transcript is permitted for the CANARY ONLY, recorded by amendment; main-question transcripts must never be regenerated

transcript_reuse.ingestion_mechanics: a phase-3 ingestion script pre-seeds the hash-chained cell-result store with rows for every transcript cell key computed under the phase-3 namespace by the same make_cell_key code path the plan enumerator uses, so the runner's completed-cell skip logic bypasses generation; a hard runtime assertion makes any attempt to reach live transcript generation for a phase-3 question a crash, never a silent provider call (see materialization_requirements.engineering_gates)

model_registry.price_note: prices are the phase-2 frozen registry values in USD per million tokens, carried forward for planning; ALL prices re-verified against a fresh provider snapshot at materialization; new-judge prices are unknown until that snapshot
model_registry.provider_revision_policy: record provider model-revision/alias metadata on every call where the API exposes it; if a pinned model id starts resolving to a new revision mid-run, halt new calls in the affected arms, record an amendment, and the owner decides continuation or exclusion; no silent alias drift

judges_new.inclusion_rule: joins if and only if it passes the canary calibration gates AND the configuration-selection procedure (decisions.configuration_selection) retains it; its retention priority in that procedure is fixed there, resolving the circularity between inclusion and fallback that the freeze consult flagged. Canary spend on a candidate that is later shed stays accrued and counted.

roster.debater_role_note: debater identity is metadata on reused transcripts; debater models are never called
roster.query_checker: google/gemma-4-31B-it under the phase-2 frozen checker config (sha256 8e674eddbb22ba73ee5a4ae4f359f1630cf4cd65c5f5d98cb70312dc868b9872)
roster.gate_reviewer: gpt-5.6-sol under the phase-2 frozen reviewer prompt (sha256 b48a125af874b287aa93e73671c9c12c9d8c4245d50e61013c690209139815f4), fresh isolated context per payload
roster.new_judge_failure_rule: a NEW judge that fails a canary calibration gate for SEMANTIC reasons (parseability, side bias) is DROPPED, not replaced (no serverless same-family substitutes exist per the 2026-08-14 availability check; no-replacement also prevents post-hoc model fishing and is submitted for explicit owner ratification). TEMPORARY endpoint unavailability or transport failure is NOT a calibration failure: those cells retry/defer under the transport policy and only an owner-recorded decision can convert persistent unavailability into a drop. A dropped new judge dissolves its within-family descriptive pair; the roster proceeds with survivors provided at least the four continuing judges remain. A CONTINUING judge failing a phase-3 gate is a halt-and-escalate to the owner, never a silent drop. All roster outcomes are recorded before any main-run outcome exists.
roster.roster_freeze_timing: the final roster (post-gates, post-configuration-selection) freezes before any capability anchor is scored and before any main-run outcome exists

debate_grid.side_assignment: K2 mirrored; labels fixed across matched conditions, identical to phase 2

tail_replicate_configurations.note: the owner selects the TARGET configuration at re-decision, informed by the v2 paired power simulation; the configuration-selection procedure may shed replicates mechanically (see decisions.configuration_selection). Replicate indices enter the seed derivation, so doubled slots are independent judge samples at temperature 0.3.

slot_arithmetic_by_roster.formula: slots = 82 x N_judges x 2 debaters x 3 transcripts x K2 x replicates(condition, config); per-judge per-condition slots are 984 at replicates 1 and 1,968 at replicates 2

debate_grid.dropped_from_phase2: batch_same_qa, placebo, capped debates, no-debate references, empty-evidence control, full-document anchors, AND with them the phase-2 secondary estimands C (cap-protection interaction) and D_clean (debate vs no-debate): all are settled phase-2 results, and phase 3 has no debater-side variation. Phase 3 is the sequential clean-oracle dose-response only.

primary_tests.confirmatory_criterion: Holm-adjusted two-sided p < 0.05 per contrast, over the family of four, is the SOLE confirmatory significance criterion for the primary family. The simultaneous band is descriptive context and is never itself used to declare or deny significance.
primary_tests.p_value_formula: per contrast j with bootstrap draw values T_j(r), r = 1..B: p_j = min(1, 2 x min[(1 + #{r: T_j(r) <= 0}) / (B + 1), (1 + #{r: T_j(r) >= 0}) / (B + 1)]) (uncentered percentile convention, identical to phase 2); Holm step-down over the four p_j with ties broken by estimand id
primary_tests.reporting: the full four-contrast vector with per-contrast 95% percentile CIs, Holm-adjusted p-values, and a descriptive simultaneous 95% sup-t band
primary_tests.sup_t_band_construction: studentized maximum-modulus on the common draws: per draw r compute m_r = max over contrasts j of |Delta_j(r) - Delta_j_hat| / se_j, where se_j is the bootstrap standard deviation of Delta_j over all draws; the 95th percentile of {m_r} is the critical value c; the band is Delta_j_hat +/- c * se_j for each j. Only B, the PRNG seed, and rounding remain for the analysis-pins artifact.
primary_tests.estimand_framing: intention-to-treat: the effect of ASSIGNMENT to up to b screened query opportunities under the frozen stopping and retry policy (the judge may answer DONE early; rejected queries consume slots per the retry rule); queries_used is post-treatment and exploratory. Public wording follows this framing.
primary_tests.downturn_scope_note: this family certifies each budget against b0 only; a downturn RELATIVE TO b2 (the pilot's U-claim) is certifiable only by the S1 secondary contrast below, never by informally comparing D8 to D2
primary_tests.population: all 82 main questions x all rostered judges x 2 debaters, subject to the D4/D8 domain override in decisions.configuration_selection if question-subsampling is reached
primary_tests.weighting: within each (question, judge, debater, condition) cell, average all slots; then equal question, judge, and debater weights; unequal slot counts across arms are a precision choice and never a weighting choice

inference.scheme: world-stratified question-cluster bootstrap with COMMON DRAWS shared by every contrast, secondary, and band: per draw r and world w, resample that world's questions with replacement (equivalently, exchangeable mean-one multinomial question weights within world); the SAME per-question weights serve every contrast in draw r
inference.domain_normalization: each contrast normalizes the weighted per-question values over ITS OWN domain with frozen domain-specific world weights: for the full domain, each world's weight is its question share of the 82; if subsampling is active for D4/D8, their domain is the frozen 41-question subset and each world's weight is its question share of the 41. The per-draw weights are shared; only the normalization domain differs. This keeps the subset's world mixture fixed across draws (random retained counts never re-randomize it) and preserves the cross-contrast covariance the sup-t band and Holm family rely on. No separate subset bootstrap is ever run.
inference.pins_remaining: B, PRNG seed, and rounding are fixed in the phase-3 analysis-pins artifact before unblinding

invalid_policy.primary: strict INVALID counts wrong (ITT; unaffected by replicate structure)
invalid_policy.principal_valid_only_sensitivity: computed on ONE FROZEN replicate index per (transcript, side) in EVERY arm (replicate index 1), so attrition is symmetric across 1-replicate and 2-replicate arms; within that single-replicate frame, slot-level common support per contrast pair: a (transcript, side) unit INVALID in either arm is dropped from both arms of that contrast
invalid_policy.descriptive_reports: an all-valid-replicates estimate (any-replicate-INVALID drops the unit) reported descriptively; INVALID counts by budget x judge x replicate block; all-INVALID-correct and all-INVALID-wrong bounds

S1_downturn_contrast.role: the single CONFIRMATORY secondary, two-sided at alpha 0.05 (family of one); it exists because the primary family cannot formally certify a downturn from b2, which is the pilot's retracted U-shape claim
S1_downturn_contrast.inference: same common draws, same p-value formula; if subsampling is active, BOTH arms restrict to the 41-question domain (paired), stated wherever S1 is reported
S1_downturn_contrast.ratification: added by the assistant on the freeze consult's finding; requires explicit owner ratification at re-decision

capability_slope.role: NOMINAL, NON-CONFIRMATORY: a finite-roster observed-score association. Its p-value is reported as nominal and no confirmatory capability claim is made from it.
capability_slope.test: the least-squares slope of per-judge D8 on the judge's centered continuous capability anchor score, across the final rostered judges
capability_slope.inference: same common question-bootstrap draws: per draw, recompute every per-judge D8 and refit the slope; the anchor score is a FIXED covariate, never resampled; two-sided percentile-bootstrap p reported as nominal
capability_slope.non_estimable_rule: with fewer than 6 rostered judges, or zero anchor-score spread, the slope is estimate-and-plot only: no p-value is reported
capability_slope.scope_of_inference: the CI is conditional on the fixed roster of judges actually run; it quantifies question-sampling uncertainty only and does NOT extend to the population of possible judge models
capability_slope.leverage_diagnostic: leave-one-judge-out refits reported as an influence diagnostic (never as a jackknife CI)
capability_slope.attenuation_disclosure: the anchor is a 48-cell binomial score (roughly 6-8pp SE per judge); classical independent measurement error TENDS TO ATTENUATE the slope IN EXPECTATION (no claim about the realized direction); no errors-in-variables correction is applied; the observed score itself is the covariate
capability_slope.parser_sensitivity_propagation: the strict-parse anchor scores are propagated through the slope: the slope is recomputed under strict-parse anchors and reported as a sensitivity

secondary_analyses.trend_test_disposition: the proposal's optional trend-test secondary is NOT exercised; any trend or shape statistic beyond S1 is descriptive only. Recorded in the authorization record as an assistant-resolved design detail, flagged for owner review.

capability_anchor.question_set: the 24 held-out calibration-excluded questions ONLY; anchor items never overlap the 82 outcome questions
capability_anchor.cells: 24 questions x K2 mirrored sides per judge, temperature 0, capability_qa prompt from the reused phase-2 prompt bundle
capability_anchor.population: ALL rostered judges are re-measured under the phase-3 manifest, continuing judges included; phase-2 anchor scores are never pooled or substituted
capability_anchor.parser_rule: PREREGISTERED TOLERANT PARSE, ratified as a NEW phase-3 rule (not inherited authority; the phase-2 parser-policy artifact is cited as precedent only): after stripping leading/trailing whitespace, exactly 'ANSWER: A' or 'ANSWER: B' with at most one optional trailing period; anything else is INVALID and counts wrong. The strict no-period parse is reported as a sensitivity and propagated per secondary_analyses.capability_slope.
capability_anchor.timing: scored and frozen after roster freeze and before any phase-3 judgment outcome exists; runs inside the canary stage under canary authorization
capability_anchor.role: the continuous covariate of the nominal capability slope; also descriptive context. Parameter count is never a capability measure. Within-family pairs and any tier split are descriptive only.

configuration_selection.purpose: ONE frozen lexicographic procedure jointly governs review-throughput feasibility, the spend cap, and Qwen3.7-Max retention, removing the circularity between the inclusion rule and the fallback

review_volume_evidence.measured_phase2: 13,753 unique-payload gate rulings (hash-chained store count) against 15,744 theoretical query slots in phase 2's two query-producing arms: 0.874 rulings per theoretical query slot, ALREADY NET of early DONE, retries, exhaustion, and dedup (never multiply it by a separate exhaustion factor; the earlier draft's [0.65, 0.94] bracket double-discounted and is retracted). Observed sustained pace: roughly 3,000 rulings per quota-day.
review_volume_evidence.planning_projections_7_judges: query-weight units per config (b1+b2+b4+b8 budgets x replicates): A=15, B=19, C=23, D=27. At the 0.874 ratio and full utilization: A roughly 90-96k rulings (30-32 quota-days), B 114-122k (38-41), C 138-147k (46-49), D 162-173k (54-58). Excludes accrued canary/anchor rulings. High-budget utilization can reach 1.00; these are planning figures, replaced by canary measurement.
review_volume_evidence.no_dedup_credit: NO credit is taken for cross-arm, cross-judge, or replicate-pair dedup in any projection or threshold decision; estimated dedup never rescues a threshold case. (If dedup materially reduces realized volume, the run simply finishes early.)

configuration_selection.trigger_metrics: blinded operational metrics only, measured in the canary: per-arm-per-judge unique-payload rulings per slot, and realized rulings per quota-day; never any efficacy quantity
configuration_selection.projection_rule: R_U = accrued canary and anchor rulings + sum over (arm, judge) of [main-run slot count x U90(unique rulings per slot for that arm and judge)], where U90 is the upper bound of a 90% confidence interval over canary per-question means (question is the cluster); D_U = ceil(R_U / L90(rulings per quota-day)), where L90 is the lower bound of a 90% interval over observed canary quota-days

limits.note: the owner selects D_max (calendar tolerance in quota-days) at re-decision; R_max is then mechanically derived as D_max x the planning pace (3,000/day) and both are frozen; the manifest enforces both R_U <= R_max and D_U <= D_max

configuration_selection.lexicographic_priority: what the design keeps, in order: (1) full 82-question coverage in every arm; (2) Qwen3.7-Max retention; (3) extra tail replicates beyond the A_no_d configuration
selection_procedure: step 0: start from the owner's target configuration and the post-gate roster; evaluate R_U, D_U, and the spend forecast
step 1: while limits are exceeded and extra tail replicates remain, shed them (b4's second replicate first, then b8's) and re-evaluate
step 2: if limits are still exceeded, shed Qwen3.7-Max (recorded with the projection arithmetic) and re-evaluate

step 3: if limits are still exceeded, restrict the b4 and b8 arms to the frozen 41-question subset (D4/D8 and S1 then use the subset domain with paired comparators per the inference pins; a descriptive curve with b0/b1/b2 ALSO restricted to the 41 is reported at no extra cost so the four points remain readable as one curve); b1 is never dropped and b1/b2/b0 never subsample
step 4: if limits are still exceeded, halt before main authorization and return to the owner; paid reviewing is NOT pre-authorized
configuration_selection.spend_cap_compliance: the same procedure and order govern the 450 USD stage cap using decisions.spend.forecast_method; whichever constraint binds first drives the same lexicographic degradation

subset_derivation.rule: half of the 82 main questions, stratified by (world, operational resolvability class), floor(n/2) per stratum plus largest-fractional-remainder to 41, lexicographic tie-break, within-stratum seeded draw without replacement in sorted-key order

query_screening.checker: the phase-2 frozen checker config, byte-identical
query_screening.retry_and_slot_policy: one free retry per attempted budget slot; a second rejection consumes the slot
query_screening.checker_failure_policy: outage, malformed output, or unresolved ambiguity halts the cell
query_screening.gate_review: the phase-2 dual-gate blinded review discipline, byte-identical reviewer prompt, unique-payload dedup documented
query_screening.audit_sampling_policy: human-review every rejection/retry and a deterministic world/resolvability-stratified 1% sample of accepted queries, blind to outcomes, unchanged from phase 2 and applied to the full phase-3 query volume; performed by the accepted_query_auditor named in external_assignments (internal QA, not an independent audit); audit reviews are outside the gate-reviewer quota and outside the throughput limits

execution_semantics.seed_policy: the phase-3 seed derivation includes question, transcript index, judge model, condition/budget, replicate index, debater model, and the protocol namespace. NOTE: phase 2's implementation (rejudge/config.py judgment_seed) omitted debater model and namespace despite its protocol text claiming otherwise; phase 3 extends the seed function to match this text (an engineering gate below), which is free of reproducibility cost because every phase-3 slot runs fresh under the new namespace.
execution_semantics.semantic_retry_policy: query-screen retry only; never regenerate an invalid verdict
execution_semantics.arm_order: randomize arm order within question; condition-balanced block scheduling so no budget arm lands systematically later under time-varying provider degradation
execution_semantics.statelessness: all judge calls stateless; caching keyed by request fingerprint; gate-review dedup by unique payload
execution_semantics.prompt_bundle: the phase-2 bundle reused byte-identical (sha256 cc02d29cfc8e7410c270c21f53da56457e44c31f74f8e512299e4e80726a076f); the sequential_judge_query template is fully parameterized by {remaining_budget}/{total_budget}, so budgets 1, 4, and 8 require no prompt changes
execution_semantics.transport_retry_policy: repeat identical request and seed; conservatively charge until provider reconciliation

launch_gates.canary_question_set: all 24 held-out questions, reused canary transcripts (zero transcript-generation cells; phase 2's canary generated transcripts, phase 3's does not)

canary_slot_inventory.per_judge_formula: core b0 gates: 24 x 2 debaters x 1 transcript x K2 = 96; budget smoke: 6 x 2 x 1 x K2 x (replicate multiplier of the target config: A=4, B=5, C=5, D=6) = 96/120/120/144; capability anchor: 24 x 2 = 48
canary_slot_inventory.totals_by_config_and_roster: total = N_judges x (96 + smoke + 48); at N7: A 1,680; B/C 1,848; D 2,016. Candidate judges that later fail gates or are shed still have their canary slots counted and their spend accrued.
canary_slot_inventory.pinned_denominator_rule: the manifest pins the exact number from this formula for the selected config and candidate roster; the completion gate uses that number

calibration_gates_per_judge.population: the 96 core b0 judgments per judge
calibration_gates_per_judge.side_bias_gate: absolute strict-error difference between the 48 A-correct and 48 B-correct mirrored judgments <= 10 percentage points per judge

launch_gates.review_volume_measurement: per-arm-per-judge unique-payload rulings per slot and realized rulings per quota-day recorded across the canary for the configuration-selection projections; Option-replicate-pair and cross-arm dedup rates recorded for information only (never credited); blinded to outcomes
launch_gates.offline_checker_fixtures: the phase-2 deterministic fixture outcomes replay green before any provider call
launch_gates.completion_gate: 100% exact completion of the manifest-pinned canary slot count (slot-level per unit_definitions)
zero_tolerance_gates: any transcript byte-mismatch against the frozen bundle
launch_gates.failure_action: halt before main spend; a semantic repair requires a new protocol ID/hash and a complete canary rerun

spend.estimate_honesty: this prose range has no computed backing yet and two large opposite-direction corrections are unmodeled: phase 3 pays ZERO debater-generation cost (which dominated phase 2's blended per-cell average), while b4/b8 slots carry up to 8 sequential oracle turns with a growing judge context re-sent each turn (super-linear per-slot token cost). A computed phase3_cost_model.json replaces this range before canary authorization; if its upper estimate exceeds 80% of the stage cap, the owner revisits the cap before canary authorization rather than discovering the squeeze mid-run.

forecast_method.formula: projected stage spend = accrued actual spend to date + sum over (model, call role, arm) of [main-run slot count x U90(tokens-in per slot) x verified input price + main-run slot count x U90(tokens-out per slot) x verified output price] x 1.15 transport-retry multiplier
forecast_method.estimator_pins: U90 = upper bound of a 90% t-interval over canary PER-QUESTION mean tokens per slot (question is the cluster; df = n_questions - 1), computed separately per (model, role, arm); zero-query and early-DONE slots enter as their actual (possibly zero) token counts, never excluded; failed and retried calls enter at their actual charged tokens; unknown or unreconciled charges count in full until provider evidence resolves them; line items ceil to whole cents
forecast_method.base_context_rule: judge-context input tokens are NOT extrapolated from the 6 smoke questions: the transcript component of every arm's input is computed exactly from the frozen main transcript bundle's per-transcript token lengths, with the canary contributing only the per-turn template and oracle-block overhead measured around those exact lengths
forecast_method.price_drift_rule: prices re-snapshot immediately before main authorization; any change from the materialization snapshot recomputes the forecast and is recorded; the method itself froze with this protocol, before any judge-specific canary cost data exists
forecast_method.executability: every input above is measurable offline or from canary artifacts, so the forecast is executable the moment the canary completes, with no free parameters

spend.controls: the amended phase-2 supervisor controls (benign-transient enumeration, uncertain-spend ceiling, same-cell cap, STOP-terminating orchestrator) carry forward; ledger, locking, reconciliation, and abnormal-resume policies inherited unchanged from phase2_protocol.json decisions.cumulative_spend

materialization_requirements.fresh_execution_identity: REQUIRED: the phase-2 identity ba017fe3... is retired by the post-phase-2 code changes; every phase-3 stage binds a new identity hash over the current frozen code bundle

provider_reconciliation.requirement: verified against the provider dashboard before canary authorization; phase-2 closed reconciled but the CURRENT figures must be re-verified, not assumed

credential_rotation.requirement: rotate the provider API key before canary authorization (the phase-2 key has since been used across many sessions); non-secret evidence recorded

role_limits.requirement: extend phase-2 v6 limits with per-model role limits and transport pins for the three new judges; transport pins are load-bearing and MUST be present for every model (rejudge/phase2_canary_manifest.py:_require_transport_pins enforces this)

cost_model.requirement: phase3_cost_model.json computed per decisions.spend.forecast_method from canary measurements plus the exact frozen transcript lengths; replaces the prose estimate before main authorization

engineering_gates_before_canary: phase3_plan.py module set: its own validate_protocol for schema_version phase3_plan_v1; enumerate_cells reading debate_grid.conditions GENERICALLY (phase 2's enumerate_canary_cells hard-codes a literal condition tuple and its validate_protocol hard-rejects any non-phase-2 protocol, so none of the phase-2 planning stack is reusable as-is); per-condition judgment replicates from the selected configuration multiplied into the replicate range (no code reads this field today); a self-test asserting per-condition slot counts against debate_grid.slot_arithmetic_by_roster before any plan is accepted
phase3 manifest modules accepting an injected protocol path (phase-2's manifest code hard-codes rejudge/phase2_protocol.json in three places)

transcript ingestion script per transcript_reuse.ingestion_mechanics, with the hard runtime assertion against live generation and the byte-mismatch zero-tolerance gate actually implemented (no code computes such a comparison today)
judgment_seed extended to include debater model and protocol namespace per decisions.execution_semantics.seed_policy, with a regression test

reproduce or bound the 2026-08-10 five-hour ssl.read hang: demonstrate the configured read timeout actually fires at the socket level under a blocked-read fault injection, or add an enforced watchdog at the transport layer
canary_supervisor subprocess.run calls carry explicit timeouts
the 30-minute stall watchdog is part of the orchestrator from the first canary block

analysis_pins.requirement: a phase-3 analysis-pins artifact fixing B, PRNG seed, rounding, and reporting decimals (the estimators, p-value formula, sup-t construction, domain normalization, INVALID mechanics, and secondary details are already pinned IN THIS PROTOCOL), frozen and independently reviewed before unblinding; the engine extends scripts/phase2_main_analysis.py and must pass a synthetic selftest with known curve values

process_commitments: design frozen and posted before launch; owner-authorized manifests and execution identities; hash-chained stores; spend caps under the amended supervisor controls; analysis pins fixed and independently reviewed before unblinding; the analysis runs once; every deviation recorded as an append-only amendment; claims stay conditional on the three worlds, the frozen transcript set, and this judge roster; the fresh b0/b2 arms are described publicly as a within-corpus retest under the phase-3 harness, never as an independent replication

external_assignments.accepted_query_auditor: internal QA: the orchestrating assistant under the owner's standing delegation; audit records tracked and owner-spot-checkable; not an independent audit
external_assignments.transcript_bundle_verifier: internal QA: the orchestrating assistant (100% sha256 coverage per transcript_reuse); verification report owner-spot-checkable
